baseline.continuous_median_rule: Fusion levels, operative time and postoperative length of stay are reported as median and interquartile range; the remaining continuous variables are reported as mean and standard deviation.
baseline.missing_stratum_handling: The discharge-timing stratum is the empty string for the patients whose postoperative length of stay is not recorded, and the label layer returns an empty string for it, so it is routed explicitly to the not-recorded label and shown as its own column rather than dropped.
baseline.scale: Within the Table 1 baseline namespace every key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, and it is a share of the analytic cohort, not of a discharge-timing stratum. The table cells themselves are rendered strings in the CSV and are authoritative for their own units. The row count is a count of TABLE ROWS and not of patients. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions in the timing step and percentages in the window step, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
baseline.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or a calendar year.
baseline.test_rule: Comparisons across the three recorded discharge-timing strata use the Kruskal-Wallis test for continuous variables and the chi-square test for categorical and binary variables. The not-recorded stratum is displayed but not tested.
bothways.inout.definition: Outpatient status defined by the billing setting, as the prior literature defines it
bothways.los.definition: Outpatient status defined by a true postoperative length of stay of zero days
bothways.no_difference_test_note: No p-value is computed for the difference between the two estimates: they are fitted on the same patients and are therefore correlated, so a two-sample comparison would be invalid.
bothways.outcome_prespec_reason: Unplanned readmission within 30 days was fixed before the first fit, for four reasons: it is the outcome the outpatient spine safety literature leads with, so re-estimating it under both exposure definitions speaks directly to the published claims the measurement critique targets; it is the most frequent adverse outcome in this cohort, so the comparison is powered to show a shift between two definitions rather than sampling noise; it is ascertained after discharge, so unlike an in-hospital complication it cannot mechanically lengthen the index stay and thereby help define the exposure it is regressed on; and it lies entirely outside the companion paper's reserved results.
bothways.scale: Within the both-ways comparison namespace every estimate and every limit is an ODDS RATIO on the ratio scale, where 1 is the null. They are NOT percentages and must never be multiplied by 100. The exposed and unexposed event rates, the event rate and the discordance are percentages on the 0 to 100 scale. The absolute difference between the two adjusted odds ratios is on the odds-ratio scale; the relative change beside it is a percentage. Every plain count in this namespace is a count of PATIENTS except the event counts, which count outcomes. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions in the timing step and percentages in the window step, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
bothways.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or a calendar year.
cif.crude_pct_note: The crude percentage is all recorded events over the analytic cohort, including any event whose postoperative day was not recorded. It is therefore greater than or equal to the day 30 estimate, and the difference is exactly the events with no recorded day over the same denominator, published as the maximum understatement for that outcome.
cif.day30_reporting_key: Report the 30-day incidence from the day 30 percentage in this namespace, with its lower and upper percentage limits. That value is the terminal point of the Figure 2 curve. Do NOT report the crude percentage as the 30-day incidence: it is a different quantity with a different numerator and it does not match the figure.
cif.identity_note: NSQIP follow-up is fixed and complete at 30 days, so nothing is censored before day 30 and the Aalen-Johansen estimator reduces algebraically to the empirical cumulative proportion of patients whose event was recorded WITH a postoperative day. It is not equal to the crude proportion of all events unless every event carried a day.
cif.scale: Within the cumulative-incidence namespace, a key ending in est, lo or hi is a proportion on the 0 to 1 scale, and a key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale. The two forms carry the same quantity and must never be mixed. The 30-day incidence a manuscript should quote is the day 30 percentage, which is also the terminal point of the Figure 2 curve. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
cif.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
cohort.flow.exclusion_arithmetic_note: The final rung removes 827 cases and the three exclusion boxes sum to 828, so 1 case meets more than one exclusion criterion. State the arithmetic; do not adjust a count to make it close.
cohort.hematoma.definition_label: Error-corrected code set plus the nervous-system hemorrhage arm
cohort.scale: Within the cohort-ladder namespace a rung count is a count of PATIENTS, a rung event count is a count of HEMATOMA events under the primary code set, and the rate beside them is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, being the events over the patients on that same rung. The exclusion boxes and the flow counts are counts of patients; the overlap count is the number of patients meeting more than one final exclusion criterion and is a count, not a difference. The two superseded code sets publish their analytic event counts here as counts of hematoma events. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
cohort.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
condrisk.scale: Within the conditional-risk namespace every curve is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, including the keys ending in est, lo and hi. Each is a list of 31 values, one per integer postoperative day 0 to 30, aligned with the day list. The difference between the two estimators is in percentage points. The conditioning-set composition lists are counts of patients on each of the same 31 days, and the in-hospital percentage is of the at-risk count on that day. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
condrisk.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
denom.ladder_source_note: Row 4 of every ladder is the sum of the frozen both-fields-recorded column that the cohort build materialised, verified here against an independent recomputation from the frozen event flag, the frozen postoperative-day column and the frozen length-of-stay column.
denom.scale: The denominator-ladder namespace carries counts of EVENTS on rows 1 to 4 and, for each row, the loss from row 1 both as a count of events and as a percentage of ROW 1 on the 0 to 100 scale. The one count of PATIENTS in this namespace is the analytic cohort size, and it is context rather than a ladder row: no percentage here is a share of the cohort. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
denom.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
derived.scale: The derived-column namespace is mostly counts of patients, and three families in it are NOT. The body-mass-index window bounds are a body mass index in kilograms per square metre. The death-day extremes are integer postoperative days, and the out-of-window day lists and the longest recorded stay among them are DAYS of postoperative stay, which are not bounded at day 30. The fusion-level cap and maximum are counts of levels operated on, not counts of patients. Every key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, and so is the completeness share spelled without that suffix. ONE key is a trap: the era-break drop in non-home discharge is a RELATIVE percentage, that is the fall expressed as a percentage of the earlier era's own rate, and it is NOT a difference in percentage points. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
derived.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
derived.scale.units: body mass index in kilograms per square metre
body mass index in kilograms per square metre
derived.slot_union.note: The primary outcome reads the first reoperation slot only, which is the convention the reconciliation gates are defined on. Reading both slots would add the cases whose hematoma reoperation was recorded as the patient's second return to theatre.
derived.subgroup.note: Ported completeness flags. This project fits no hematoma risk model and no burden analysis; the flags exist so the two cohorts carry the same columns.
derived.trach.identified_only_note: Measured on the wider identified cohort the two readings differ on a small number of patients, every one of whom the cohort definition excludes before any analysis sees them. That figure is published unadjusted rather than suppressed, but it does not bear on the composite, which is only ever computed on the analytic cohort.
derived.trach.invariant_note: On the analytic cohort the composite airway outcome is identical whether the tracheostomy arm reads reoperation slot 1 only or slots 1 and 2, because every slot-2 tracheostomy there already enters the composite through unplanned reintubation or prolonged ventilation. The composite therefore stays on the parent's frozen slot-1 implementation and the two papers cannot disagree about it.
dest.home_definition: Home discharge is taken from the explicit destination level map, which maps the level meaning a facility that had been the patient's residence to the facility group. It is never defined by matching the word Home.
dest.note: The discharge destination vocabulary changes completely at the era break, collapsing from seven facility levels to two, so the non-home discharge rate is not comparable across the break. The distribution is reported by year because the plan requires it, and no claim that non-home discharge declined is made anywhere in this manuscript.
dest.scale: Within the discharge-destination namespace every key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale. The era-break year is a calendar year. No trend claim may be attached to any of these percentages: the destination vocabulary changes completely at the era break. The count of distinct destination levels observed in an era is a count of VOCABULARY LEVELS and not a count of patients, and it is the measurement that makes the era break visible. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions in the timing step and percentages in the window step, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
dest.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or a calendar year.
dest.scale.units: count of distinct discharge destination levels
dq.carryover.owner_note: 03_timing.py owns the published median postoperative day and the day 0 to 1 share; 04_postdischarge.py owns the published post-discharge fraction. These keys are the reconciliation of the carried-over figures against their unrecorded denominators, and they are not the published values.
dq.carryover.postdisch.note: PLAN.md section 13 lists the denominator behind the carried-over 41.3% as an open item. Measured here from the frozen columns across every rung and both code sets. 04_postdischarge.py owns the published figure and must re-derive it; the manuscript reports the analytic-cohort value whatever this reconciliation says, because the analytic cohort is the study population (CLAUDE.md 4.4). A mismatch is reported, not overwritten in either direction (CLAUDE.md 8.5).
dq.expired.note: A patient recorded as having expired before discharge has no discharge day. These patients are the competing event in the Aalen-Johansen estimator and must never be read as same-day discharges. Both directions of the reconciliation are published: expired patients without a recorded death day, and recorded deaths whose discharge destination is not expired, which are the patients who died after discharge.
dq.negflag_days.airway.reason: the composite reads the reoperation day for the tracheostomy arm, and that field is recorded for every unplanned reoperation
dq.negflag_days.death.reason: no documented reason: an unexpected value here is a data-quality finding
dq.negflag_days.hematoma.reason: the reoperation day is recorded for every unplanned reoperation, and most reoperations are not hematoma evacuations
dq.negflag_days.pneumonia.reason: no documented reason: an unexpected value here is a data-quality finding
dq.negflag_days.readmit.reason: the readmission day is recorded for planned readmissions as well as unplanned ones
dq.negflag_days.reintub.reason: no documented reason: an unexpected value here is a data-quality finding
dq.negflag_days.reop_any.reason: no documented reason: an unexpected value here is a data-quality finding
dq.negflag_days.vent48.reason: no documented reason: an unexpected value here is a data-quality finding
dq.scale: The data-quality namespace publishes counts of patients, counts of hematoma events on the carried-over reconciliations, and percentages on the 0 to 100 scale. TWO families carry a unit their name does not. The carried-over reoperation day, both the plan's own figure and the value re-derived on each rung, is an integer POSTOPERATIVE DAY published under a bare name with no unit in it. The carried-over share on the same rungs is a percentage, and the opposite-tie variant beside it is a percentage on the same denominator and not a difference. Nothing in this namespace is a published result: these are reconciliations against the carried-over figures, and the timing step and the post-discharge step own the published values. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
dq.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
dq.second_event.note: Only the first event of each type is timed in the analyses. A second reoperation and a second through fifth readmission carry their own day fields and are counted here; a third reoperation carries none. All analyses are time-to-first-event, pre-specified.
era.pooling_verdict: No outcome carries a step at the coding transition, so every timing curve is reported pooled across 2012 to 2024.
era.rule: A step is declared when the last pre-transition year and the first transition year differ at p below 0.05 by a two-sided Fisher exact test AND the absolute change at that boundary is the largest of the twelve adjacent-year changes. An outcome with a step is reported by era and never pooled.
era.scale: Within the coding-era namespace, a key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale and a key ending in pp is a difference between two such percentages, expressed in percentage points. Year keys are calendar years. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
era.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
gate.1.detail: both ladders re-counted on the already-derived frame with the added column dropped: identical; both ladders rebuilt from the raw CSV with the added column deleted before any derivation ran: identical, and the added column is provably never read outside its own column build
gate.1.export_proof: T1, .build_facts.md 7.1: 124,344 rows compared, 0 rows differing, column order identical after removing the added column, SHA-256 identical.
gate.1.note: Adding the billing-setting column to the variable list moved no row count. The cohort ladder reproduces the pinned constants exactly on the widened bundle; both ladders rebuild identically from the raw CSV with the added column deleted before any derivation runs, so no eligibility predicate and no upstream derivation reads it; and the export layer separately proved this bundle is the parent's bundle plus exactly one column, row for row.
gate.1.structural_postderive_detail: both ladders re-counted on the already-derived frame with the added column dropped: identical
gate.1.structural_rebuild_detail: both ladders rebuilt from the raw CSV with the added column deleted before any derivation ran: identical, and the added column is provably never read outside its own column build
gate.a.note: Reconciliation only. The delta is exactly the top-coded-age patients the plan's strict integer cast nulls, and it carries zero hematoma events. Its output belongs to the ascertainment supplement and never to the manuscript body.
gate.b.note: Every rung and every event count asserted against cpt_acdf.COHORT_LADDER_N and COHORT_LADDER_EVENTS. No count is retyped in this step, and the verdict key is computed from that comparison rather than written as a constant.
gate.scale: Within the gate namespace the reconciliation ladder carries the same three families as the primary ladder: a count of PATIENTS, a count of HEMATOMA events, and a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale. The rungs-checked count is a number of comparisons, not of patients. The column-width keys are counts of COLUMNS in the export bundle, and the rows-moved key is a count of patients, which is zero by design. Every verdict key is a boolean. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
gate.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
gray.method: Gray's k-sample test on the cumulative incidence functions, rho = 0. Follow-up is complete to day 30, so every inverse-probability-of-censoring weight is one and the statistic is the multivariate log-rank form computed on subdistribution risk sets.
gray.scale: Within the stratum-comparison namespace, a stratum-level day 30 cumulative incidence is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, and it is withheld where the stratum carries fewer events than the suppression rule allows. The statistic is a chi-square value on its own degrees of freedom. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
gray.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
gray.strata_proportions_suppressed_list: Death within 30 days, Age group 18–49 years, 7 events in 34,191 patients
gray.suppression.proportion_rule: A stratum-level day 30 cumulative incidence computed on fewer than 10 events is withheld rather than reported. The stratum size, the event count and the denominator are still published, so the suppression is auditable, and each withheld cell carries its own suppression flag. A reader cannot be expected to check an event count before quoting a percentage.
gray.suppression.rule: A stratum with fewer than 10 events of the outcome is excluded from the test and reported with its count. A comparison left with fewer than two strata is not tested and its p value is null.
inout.primary_form: The year-by-year statistics are the primary form. The pooled statistic is reported only beside them, because the raw billing column steps twice inside the study window and a pooled figure would hide both steps.
inout.reconcile.note: The manuscript reports the billing-label analysis on the analytic cohort. The pre-exclusion figures exist only so the carried-over count can be reconciled, and none of them is a denominator for a reported percentage.
inout.replication_note: This measurement critique is a replication and extension of a published analysis of the same billing field on ACDF in the same registry. It is never described as new, novel or first. What extends it is the window carried to 2024, the larger measured sample, the year-by-year agreement and kappa, and the diagnostic-accuracy framing.
inout.scale: Within the billing-label agreement namespace, agreement, disagreement, sensitivity, specificity and both predictive values are PERCENTAGES on the 0 to 100 scale, and so are their lower and upper limits. Kappa is the one exception: it and its limits and its standard error are a Cohen kappa on the minus 1 to 1 scale and are NOT a percentage. Multiplying a kappa by 100 is the single easiest mistake to make in this namespace, and it is the reason the year-by-year and went-home families are enumerated key by key rather than written as a prefix: the smallest and the largest kappa each carry the YEAR they occurred in, which is a calendar year and not a percentage, and the went-home sensitivity family holds a kappa and a count of patients beside its percentages. The reconciliation rungs publish an outpatient count, a stayed-a-night count and the percentage between them for every gate and rung, and only the third of those is a percentage. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions in the timing step and percentages in the window step, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
inout.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or a calendar year.
inout.step_change_note: The share of cases carrying the outpatient billing label steps at two points inside the window, and the later step coincides with the discharge destination vocabulary change. A change in a billing label is not read as a change in practice anywhere in this manuscript.
inoutfield.note: The billing setting is not a discharge measure and is never used as one. True same-day discharge is derived from the postoperative length-of-stay field. 05_inout.py owns the agreement analysis and the reconciliation of the carried-over outpatient count; these keys are the column build only.
inoutfield.scale: The billing-label namespace publishes counts of PATIENTS and one percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, which is the outpatient share of the analytic cohort. The billing setting is not a discharge measure and none of these keys is a length of stay. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
inoutfield.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
ladder.scale: The outcome-variant namespace publishes ONE numeric family and it is a count of hematoma events on a cohort rung under one of the three code sets. There is no patient count and no percentage in this namespace, so a rate must never be read from it; the matching patient counts live on the cohort ladder. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
ladder.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
ladder.variant.v0.label: Original code set, retained as a sensitivity analysis
ladder.variant.v1.label: Error-corrected code set, hematoma arm only
ladder.variant.v2.label: Error-corrected code set plus the nervous-system hemorrhage arm
los.exclusion_rule: A patient with an expired discharge destination, a recorded death within 30 days, or a still in hospital flag did not go home and is excluded from the discharge-timing rates that carry the exclusion label. Both forms are reported.
los.gate2.note: Every carried-over figure is re-derived on the analytic cohort, which is the population every other number in this manuscript uses. A mismatch is reported, never overwritten in either direction.
los.gate2.reconcile.note: The carried-over discharge-timing figures were measured on the pre-exclusion population, not on the analytic cohort. The manuscript reports the analytic figure with its denominator and states the reconciliation; neither value is overwritten.
los.primary_field_note: Every discharge definition in this step is derived from the days from operation to discharge field and never from the billing setting.
los.scale: Within the postoperative length-of-stay namespace, a key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale. The distribution keys are DAYS of postoperative stay and are NOT bounded at day 30: the maximum in this cohort is 112 days and 74 patients stayed past day 30, so the timing rule that bounds an event day at 30 must never be applied to a length of stay. Two denominators run in parallel through this namespace: the rate on every patient whose length of stay is recorded, and the companion rate on the smaller denominator that excludes the patients who did not go home. Both are percentages, they are not interchangeable, and each is published with its own numerator and its own denominator beside it. The reconciliation rungs carry their own same-day and by-day-1 rates, also percentages, measured on the pre-exclusion population rather than on the analytic cohort. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions in the timing step and percentages in the window step, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
los.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or a calendar year.
losfield.discharge_contamination_note: SAMEDAY_DISCH and DISCH_BY_POD1 are defined on the postoperative length-of-stay field alone and their definitions are deliberately unchanged, because 05_inout.py needs the raw form for the agreement analysis. They therefore contain patients who did not go home: an expired discharge destination, a recorded death within 30 days, or a still-in-hospital flag. Binding on 05_inout.py: exclude them explicitly and state the exclusion, rather than reporting a same-day-discharge rate that counts deaths as discharges.
losfield.scale: Within the length-of-stay namespace the distribution keys, the disagreement deltas and the listed stays are DAYS of postoperative stay, and they are NOT bounded at day 30: the maximum here is 112 days, so the rule that bounds an event day at 30 must never be applied to a length of stay. Everything else is a count of patients, except the disagreement rate, which is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale of the rows where both fields are present, and the three still-in-hospital scoring keys, which count EVENTS rather than patients. ONE key is a trap: the count of patients whose recorded postoperative stay was zero is spelled as though it were a number of days and is a number of PATIENTS. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
losfield.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
losfield.stillinhosp_bounding_note: Binding on 04_postdischarge.py: these are the patients the bounding sensitivity must be conditioned on. A patient never discharged inside the follow-up window cannot have had an event after a discharge that did not occur, so the STILLINHOSP-conditioned bound is the primary one and the naive unconditional bound may be shown only beside it, labelled as such.
losfield.stillinhosp_note: The still-in-hospital flag means the patient was still admitted beyond 30 days after the operation. It does NOT mean the patient has no length of stay and it must not be described that way: most carry no length-of-stay value, but the rest do, some of them 30 days or fewer, and the ones whose event day and length of stay are both present are already inside 04's row-4 denominators, every one of them scored pre-discharge. The sub-counts are published as their own keys so a downstream step reads numbers rather than this sentence.
missing.note_event_rate_versus_missingne: The database-wide percentages carried in the plan for each days-to-event field are EVENT RATES, not missingness rates: a days-to-event field is populated only for patients who had the event. The quantity that matters, and that was unmeasured before this project, is the missingness of the days-to-event field CONDITIONAL on the event flag being positive, which is what this supplement reports.
missing.scale: The conditional-missingness namespace publishes counts of EVENTS and percentages on the 0 to 100 scale, and every one of those percentages is CONDITIONAL ON THE EVENT HAVING FIRED: the denominator is that outcome's ladder row 1, never the analytic cohort and never a database-wide rate. An event rate and a missingness rate are different quantities and this namespace holds only the second. The one count of PATIENTS is the number flagged still in hospital beyond the follow-up window. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
missing.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
postdisch.bound_denominator_note: Both bounds place the events that the complete-case analysis could not place, so both are computed on ladder row 1. The point estimate in Table 3B row 5 is computed on ladder row 4. The two denominators differ on purpose, so a point estimate may sit outside its own conditioned interval; that is the bounding argument working, not an error.
postdisch.bound_primary_rule: The still-in-hospital conditioned bound is the primary bounding sensitivity. Every event lost because the postoperative length of stay is missing belongs to a patient flagged still in hospital beyond 30 days, and such a patient was never discharged inside the follow-up window, so the event cannot have occurred after a discharge that did not occur. The unconditional extreme is reported beside it for comparison only and is structurally impossible for those rows.
postdisch.death.tie_note: For a patient who died in hospital the recorded postoperative length of stay is the day of the terminal event, so the opposite tie convention would score that patient as having died after a discharge that never happened. The locked convention scores them before discharge, which is correct. Death's opposite-convention figure must never be quoted without this reason.
postdisch.hematoma.carryover.note: The carried-over figure is an identified-cohort number. This manuscript reports the analytic-cohort value with its denominator, because the analytic cohort is the study population, and states the identified-rung reconciliation beside it. The carried-over figure was also measured under the superseded hematoma code set, so a small movement against the current primary definition is expected and is quantified here rather than asserted.
postdisch.readmit.day_before_discharge_n: The readmission day is counted from the principal operation and the length of stay is the day of discharge from the index admission, so a readmission day strictly before the discharge day is internally contradictory. These rows are counted and reported, never corrected and never dropped. They are a further reason the readmission post-discharge fraction is not reported as a result.
postdisch.readmit_excluded_reason: The days-to-readmission field counts from the principal operation, so an unplanned readmission is a post-discharge event by construction for anyone who was discharged. Its post-discharge fraction is uninformative and is not reported as a result; the timing curve shape is reported instead.
postdisch.scale: Within the post-discharge namespace every key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale and every key ending in pp is a difference between two such percentages, expressed in percentage points. Every plain count is a count of EVENTS, never of patients: a denominator here is the number of events with both the day and the length of stay recorded, and a stratum cell counts events inside that stratum. The point estimate is a percentage of ladder ROW 4 while both bounds are percentages of ladder ROW 1, so the two share a unit and do NOT share a denominator, which is why a point estimate may legitimately sit outside its own conditioned interval. The bounding threshold is a percentage of row 1. The minimum stratum denominator is a COUNT of events and is the suppression threshold, not a measured quantity. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
postdisch.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
postdisch.strata_suppressed_list: Death within 30 days, Age group 18–49 years, denominator 7
postdisch.strata_suppression_rule: A stratum whose analysis denominator, that is its own ladder row 4, is fewer than 10 events has its proportion withheld rather than reported. The counts are published so the suppression is auditable.
postdisch.tie_convention: An event recorded on the same postoperative day as discharge counts as occurring before discharge.
postdisch.tie_convention_sensitivity: An event recorded on the same postoperative day as discharge counts as occurring after discharge.
prespec.censoring: administrative at day 30, non-informative, complete by construction
prespec.composite_timing: the earliest observed postoperative day among the components that fired
prespec.estimator: Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence function with death as the competing event, not one minus Kaplan-Meier
prespec.mortality_sensitivity: DOPERTOD or YRDEATH, never called 30-day mortality
prespec.scale: The pre-specification namespace is mostly locked text. Its ONE trap is the risk threshold list, which is held as PROPORTIONS on the 0 to 1 scale, with a matching list of rendered percentage labels beside it; multiplying a label by 100 or reading a threshold as a percentage is the error this declaration exists to prevent. The follow-up length is a number of days, the timing range bounds are integer postoperative days, the suppression rule is a count of EVENTS, the bootstrap size is a count of replicates, and the seed is a dimensionless integer that is not a measurement of anything. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
prespec.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
prespec.scale.units: dimensionless integer, a seed and not a measurement
prespec.stratum_comparison: Gray's test on the cumulative incidence functions
prespec.suppression_rule: a stratum with fewer than 10 composite events is suppressed rather than plotted, and the suppression is reported with its count
prespec.tie_convention: An event recorded on the same postoperative day as discharge counts as occurring before discharge.
prespec.tie_convention_sensitivity: An event recorded on the same postoperative day as discharge counts as occurring after discharge.
prespec.time_zero: the day of the principal operation, postoperative day 0
prespec.timing_out_of_range_rule: A days-to-event value is used only when it is an integer in the range 0 to 30 postoperative days. Any other value is counted, published with its field, and set to missing in the derived postoperative-day column. It is never clipped to a boundary and never silently dropped: the patient stays in the cohort and stays an event, and only the timing is treated as unobserved.
prespec.tracheostomy_slot: reoperation slot 1 only inside the composite, the parent's frozen implementation; the slots 1 and 2 marker is ascertainment supplement only
prespec.window_composite: WINDOW_COMP = HEMATOMA OR REINTUBATION OR VENT48 OR REOP_TRACH
s3.death.note: Death has no competing event, so the Aalen-Johansen estimator reduces to the ordinary cumulative incidence and the two estimators are identical by construction. The row is printed to show that, not as a comparison.
s3.method: One minus Kaplan-Meier treats a competing death as non-informative censoring, which assumes the patient who died would have gone on to experience the complication at the same rate as the living. It therefore overstates the cumulative incidence of every non-fatal outcome. The size of the correction is measured here rather than assumed small.
s3.scale: Within the competing-risk-correction namespace every estimate and limit is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, the absolute difference between the two estimators is in percentage points, and the relative difference is a percentage of the Aalen-Johansen value. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
s3.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
suppress.residual_level_rule: A stratum level that is not one of the stratifier's declared levels is labelled from the column that carries the recorded value, through the label layer, and is called not recorded only when the value is genuinely unrecorded. Its fragment key segment is frozen at the residual name and is never rendered.
suppress.scale: The suppression namespace carries no risk and no percentage. Every numeric key in it is a count of patients or events, or the minimum event count the suppression rule applies. The level keys carry the display label of a suppressed stratum and whether the stratifier value behind it is recorded. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
suppress.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
timing.censoring: administrative at postoperative day 30, non-informative, and complete by construction: NSQIP follow-up is fixed at 30 days and there is no loss to follow-up in the ordinary sense
timing.ci.method: 95% limits from the Klein-Moeschberger delta-method variance with the log-log transformation, so both limits stay inside the unit interval
timing.death.no_competing_event: For death itself there is no competing event and the Aalen-Johansen estimator reduces to the ordinary cumulative incidence.
timing.estimator: Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence function with death as the competing event, evaluated as a step function on integer postoperative days
timing.estimator.implementation: written out directly over 31 integer time points; the lifelines fitter was not used because it jitters tied event times and drops every event at time 0
timing.gate2.note: The carried-over figures were measured under the superseded hematoma code set on the identified rung. The analytic value is primary and the identified value is the reconciliation. A difference is a documented movement of definition and denominator, not a number to overwrite.
timing.gate2.verdict: median postoperative day reproduces on the analytic rung: True; median reproduces on the identified rung: True; day 0 to 1 share reproduces on the analytic rung to one decimal: False; day 0 to 1 share reproduces on the identified rung to one decimal: True
timing.library.note: A library-behaviour diagnostic, never an estimate. It records what the lifelines Aalen-Johansen fitter would have returned on the same time and event-type vectors, which is lower than the exact value because that implementation drops the events at time 0. Its event table always carries a synthesised time-0 row, the lagged survival is undefined on that row and is zeroed, and the events sitting on it therefore never reach the running sum. Events at a later earliest observed time are not affected. In this cohort time 0 is the earliest observed time on every outcome and day 0 carries real events on every outcome, so the loss is real here; the mechanism is stated as time 0 rather than as the earliest observed time because only the former generalises.
timing.scale: Within the descriptive-timing namespace, a key ending in pct is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale and a key ending in pp is a difference expressed in percentage points. A postoperative day is an integer day count from the principal operation. Postoperative length of stay is NOT bounded at day 30 and runs to 112 days in this cohort. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
timing.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
timing.second_event.note: All analyses are time to first event. NSQIP records a days to event field for occurrence 1 in every family, a second reoperation and a second through fifth readmission, and nothing beyond, so a third reoperation carries no timing at all.
timing.tie_convention: An event recorded on the same postoperative day as discharge counts as occurring before discharge.
timing.time_zero: the day of the principal operation, postoperative day 0
timing.trach.in_composite: slot 1 only, the companion project's frozen implementation
timingfield.los_rule_note: The 0 to 30 day rule applies to days-to-event fields only. Length of stay is not a window-bounded quantity: a patient may legitimately stay in hospital for more than 30 days, and truncating a length of stay would corrupt the discharge-timing analysis this project exists to do.
timingfield.loss_bounding_handoff: Binding on 04_postdischarge.py: report the STILLINHOSP-conditioned bound as the primary bounding sensitivity, and show the naive unconditional bound only beside it, labelled as the unconditional extreme.
timingfield.loss_decomposition_note: The loss between rows 1 and 4 of the PLAN.md 6.2 denominator ladder is decomposed into three disjoint reasons: the days-to-event field is missing; the length of stay is missing on a patient flagged still in hospital beyond 30 days; and the length of stay is missing on a patient not so flagged. Nothing is reclassified and no ladder count moves. The split exists because a patient who was never discharged inside the follow-up window cannot have had the event after a discharge that did not occur, so for those rows the 'all missing events post-discharge' extreme is structurally impossible rather than merely conservative.
timingfield.rule: A days-to-event value is used only when it is an integer in the range 0 to 30 postoperative days. Any other value is counted, published with its field, and set to missing in the derived postoperative-day column. It is never clipped to a boundary and never silently dropped: the patient stays in the cohort and stays an event, and only the timing is treated as unobserved.
timingfield.scale: The pre-flight namespace holds two different kinds of key. Per OUTCOME, every count is a count of EVENTS on the denominator ladder and every key ending in pct is a percentage of that outcome's own row 1, on the 0 to 100 scale. Per FIELD, the minimum, the maximum, the observed value list and the list of values absent from the window are DAYS, and the counts beside them are counts of patients carrying that field. A days-to-event field is bounded to 0 to 30 by the handling rule; a length-of-stay field is NOT bounded and runs to 112 days here, and the field's own family key says which of the two it is. The window bounds themselves are integer postoperative days and the bounding threshold is a percentage. The per-field drop counts are counts of PATIENTS, one row each, but the total beside them is summed across eleven fields and is therefore a count of VALUES, not of distinct patients. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, percentages, odds ratios and a kappa in the analysis steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
timingfield.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
timingfield.scale.units: count of recorded values, summed across fields
trend.covid_note: The pandemic year is plotted and annotated rather than smoothed, and the trend is reported with and without it.
trend.disch_by_pod1.endpoint_difference_: The endpoint difference is the last observed year minus the first observed year. It is a description of two points, not a fitted quantity, and it is not the fitted slope multiplied by the window: the two agree only on a perfectly linear series. Report whichever one the sentence is actually about, name it as what it is, and do not present one as the other.
trend.logit.year_term: operative year as a linear term, per additional year
trend.sameday.endpoint_difference_note: The endpoint difference is the last observed year minus the first observed year. It is a description of two points, not a fitted quantity, and it is not the fitted slope multiplied by the window: the two agree only on a perfectly linear series. Report whichever one the sentence is actually about, name it as what it is, and do not present one as the other.
trend.scale: Within the discharge-timing trend namespace the logistic model publishes an ODDS RATIO per additional operative year, with its two limits on the same ratio scale; they are not percentages. Everything else is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, except the fitted Cochran-Armitage slope, the fitted change across the window and the endpoint difference, which are in PERCENTAGE POINTS. A slope in percentage points per year and an endpoint difference in percentage points are different quantities and must not be presented as one another. The first, last and peak year of a series are CALENDAR YEARS; the percentage that goes with each of them carries the same stem with a percentage suffix, and the two must never be swapped. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions in the timing step and percentages in the window step, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
trend.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or a calendar year.
trend.scale.units: count of year gaps, one fewer than the number of years
window.bootstrap.reason: The conditional risk is a ratio functional of two Aalen-Johansen quantities and has no closed-form Aalen-Johansen variance, so the pre-specified seeded bootstrap applies
window.competing_tie_rule: Where the composite event and death fall on the same postoperative day the composite is taken as the first event
window.composite.definition: Hematoma requiring unplanned reoperation, unplanned reintubation, ventilator dependence beyond 48 hours, or reoperative tracheostomy. Pneumonia and unplanned readmission are excluded.
window.estimand: The earliest postoperative day at which the conditional probability of a subsequent composite event, given the patient is event free and alive at the start of that day, falls below the threshold
window.estimator: Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence with death as the competing event
window.indexing_rule: An event recorded on postoperative day D is counted as still ahead of a patient discharged on day D, so the conditioning set is the patients event free and alive at the start of day D
window.riskset.definition: A patient is counted as still in hospital at the start of postoperative day D when the recorded postoperative length of stay had not ended before day D, that is when the length of stay is at least D. A patient discharged on day D was in hospital at the start of it, which is the same day indexing the estimand uses.
window.riskset.flag_rule: The still-in-hospital flag is never used to override a recorded length of stay, because it is not equivalent to one: some flagged patients carry a recorded stay. It is reported only as how many of the patients with no recorded stay are known to have been in hospital at the end of the window.
window.riskset.missing_stay_rule: Postoperative length of stay is not recorded for a small number of patients, who cannot be placed on either side. They are counted separately on every day, the primary still-in-hospital count excludes them, and an upper bound that places every one of them in hospital is published beside it.
window.riskset.text.caveat: Because the conditioning set at each day is overwhelmingly made up of patients who had already gone home, the safe discharge day must not be described as the observation a patient needs, as a period a patient must be watched for, or as a length of stay. It is the day on which the probability of a subsequent qualifying event first falls below the stated threshold, estimated on a cohort in which almost every patient still at risk on that day was already at home.
window.riskset.text.methods: The conditional risk at postoperative day D is estimated on every patient who is event free and alive at the start of that day, whether or not that patient was still in hospital. Membership of the conditioning set is a survival condition and not an observation condition, so the quantity is the probability that a qualifying event is still ahead of a patient on day D and is not an estimate of the effect of continued inpatient observation. The composition of the conditioning set is reported on every day so that the estimand cannot be read as an observation effect.
window.riskset.text.missing_handling: Postoperative length of stay is not recorded for 83 patients, of whom 77 carry the still-in-hospital flag and are therefore known to have been in hospital at the end of the window, while 6 cannot be placed. They are counted as not still in hospital in the primary count, and the bound that places every one of them in hospital is reported beside it. The flag itself never overrides a recorded stay: 35 of the 112 flagged patients carry one.
window.riskset.text.results: Most of the patients the conditional risk is measured on had already been discharged: 13,530 of the 112,114 patients event free and alive at the start of postoperative day 3 were still in hospital (12.1%), 2,647 of the 111,857 patients event free and alive at the start of postoperative day 7 were still in hospital (2.4%), and 542 of the 111,651 patients event free and alive at the start of postoperative day 14 were still in hospital (0.5%).
window.scale: Within the safe-discharge-window namespace EVERY risk is a percentage on the 0 to 100 scale, including the keys ending in est, lo and hi. The three keys that carry a residual risk at a threshold are a percentage and its two percentage limits, even though only the first of the three is suffixed with pct. A safe discharge day and its limits are integer postoperative days, null where the threshold is not reached inside the window. The threshold list itself is the exception and is held as proportions on the 0 to 1 scale, with a matching list of rendered labels beside it. The conditioning-set composition keys are counts of patients and their percentages of the at-risk denominator on the same day. This declaration governs only the namespace it is named for. It is not a project-wide rule and must never be read as one: the same est, lo and hi suffixes carry proportions, odds ratios and a kappa in other steps, so read the declaration published by the step that owns the key.
window.scale.other_numeric_keys: Every other numeric key in this namespace is a count of patients or events, a denominator, or an integer day.
window.scale.units: random number generator seed, carries no unit
